newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht recovers late, interbank rate higher.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht recovers late, interbank rate higher.

text.p: The Thai baht recovered late on Thursday against the dollar after a morning as investors sold the U.S. unit to take profits from recent gains, dealers said.
Stop-loss selling of the dollar were also seen as the recently-surging greenback corrected against the yen and mark, dealers said.
The baht firmed to 25.808-25.818 to the dollar late from 25.822-25.827 earlier and 25.798-25.808 late on Wednesday.
"I heard the baht was traded as low as 25.830 in the morning on heavy buying of the dollar," said one dealer at a local bank.
"Dollar selling was seen in the afternoon. Dollar's weakness against major currencies and profit taking prompted the dollar selling," the dealer added.
The Bank of Thailand's denial of fresh baht devaluation rumours in the morning also made speculators cautious about central bank intervention, dealers said.
"For my bank, there was no intervention by central bank. I don't know about other banks," said another dealer at a major local bank.
The bid/offer range of one-month baht/dollar swap premium rose to 9.30/9.90 per a dollar early from 9.25/9.75 late on Wednesday.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the baht/dollar mid-rate at 25.79, the lowest level since August 20, 1991 when the mid-rate was set at 25.82. The mid-rate was at 25.75 on Wednesday.
The strong buying of the dollar pushed the overnight interbank rate higher to 10.00-10.50 percent in late trade from 9.00-9.50 in the morning and 8.00-8.50 late on Wednesday, dealers said.
"If there was stronger buying of the dollar in the afternoon, the interbank rate might have reached 12.00 percent," said another dealer at a foreign bank.
